'''Annette Jane Dobson''' {{postnominals|country=AUS|AM}} (born 4 September 1945) is an Australian statistician. She is a Professor of [[Biostatistics]] in the [[University of Queensland]]'s Australian Women and Girl's Health Research (AWaGHR) Centre in the School of Public Health.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Annette Dobson |url=https://researchers.uq.edu.au/researcher/854 |access-date=2022-06-23 |website=University of Queensland}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Prof Annette Dobson |url=http://www.acithn.uq.edu.au/staff/StaffSearch/staff_profile.asp?staff_id%3D53 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091003085216/http://www.acithn.uq.edu.au/staff/StaffSearch/staff_profile.asp?staff_id=53 |archive-date=2009-10-03 |website=University of Queensland}}</ref> Dobson was Director of the Australian Longitudinal Study on Women's Health from 1995 to 2013.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date= |title=ALSWH Steering Committee: Professor Annette Dobson AO |url=http://www.alswh.org.au/Staff/annette.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120320132611/http://www.alswh.org.au/Staff/annette.html |archive-date=2012-03-20 |access-date= |website=Women's Health Australia (WHA)}}</ref> She is a highly cited publication author,<ref>{{cite web |title=Core Research |url=http://www.sph.uq.edu.au/core-research |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100501003119/http://sph.uq.edu.au/core-research |archive-date=2010-05-01 |website=School of Population Health, The University of Queensland}}</ref> a book author,<ref>{{Cite book |last=Dobson |first=Annette J. |title=An Introduction to Generalized Linear Models |publisher=CRC Press |year=1990 |language=en}}</ref> and has received an Australia Day award.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2010-01-27 |title=UQ recipients in Australia Day Honours List |url=https://www.uq.edu.au/news/article/2010/01/uq-recipients-australia-day-honours-list |access-date=2022-06-23 |website=UQ News, University of Queensland |language=en}}</ref>

== Qualification ==
Dobson has a bachelor's degree from the [[University of Adelaide]], and a master's degree and PhD from [[James Cook University]]. She has a postgraduate diploma in management from the [[University of New England (Australia)]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://researchers.uq.edu.au/researcher/854|title=Professor Annette Dobson|work=Researchers|publisher=University of Queensland|access-date=2024-05-21}}</ref>

== Research interests ==
Her research interests lie in the fields of biostatistics, [[epidemiology]], [[longitudinal studies]], and [[social determinants of health]]. In biostatistics, she is specifically interested in [[generalized linear model]]ing, [[clinical biostatistics]], and statistical methods in [[longitudinal studies]]. Dobson's topics in epidemiology include [[tobacco control]], [[diabetes]], [[cardiovascular disease]], [[obesity]] and health care service use.

== Positions ==
Dobson is the founding Director of the Australian Longitudinal Study on Women's Health (ALSWH)<ref name=":0" /> and was director of the Centre for Longitudinal and Life Course Research from 2012 - 2021.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sph.uq.edu.au/centre-for-longitudinal-and-life-course-research |title=Centre for Longitudinal and Life Course Research - School of Population Health - the University of Queensland, Australia |accessdate=2015-03-14 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150227232210/http://www.sph.uq.edu.au/centre-for-longitudinal-and-life-course-research |archivedate=27 February 2015 |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

She was the inaugural chair of the [[BCA Master of Biostatistics]] at its inception in 2000.

== Awards ==
Dobson was made a Member of the Order of Australia in 2010 for her service to [[public health]] and biostatistics as a research and academic, particularly through the collection and analysis of data relating to cardiovascular disease and women's and veterans' health, which provided a basis for public health interventions and policies to reduce [[disease burden]] in the population.<ref>{{cite web| title=Dobson, Annette Jane| publisher= It's an Honour| url=https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/1141749 |accessdate= 19 February 2010}}</ref>

Dobson won the Sidney Sax medal in 2003, the pre-eminent prize awarded by the Public Health Association of Australia.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.phaa.net.au/scholarships-awards/awards/sidney-sax-public-health-medal-sidney-sax-public-health-medal-nominations-for-the-sidney-sax-public-health-medal-for-2015-have-closed-please-do-not-hesitate-to-email-phaaphaanetau-for-further-informat |accessdate= 8 August 2018|title= Sidney Sax Public Health Medal - Public Health Association of Australia Inc}}</ref>  Dobson received the 2012 Moyal Medal for her contributions to statistics<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://maths.mq.edu.au/medal/lecture2012.html |title=Moyal medallists |access-date=14 March 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150323104332/https://maths.mq.edu.au/medal/lecture2012.html |archive-date=23 March 2015 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref> and in 2015 she was elected Fellow of the [[Australian Academy of Health and Medical Sciences]] (FAHMS).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.aahms.org/fellowship/|title=Fellowship {{!}} AAHMS – Australian Academy of Health and Medical Sciences|website=www.aahms.org|language=en-AU|access-date=2018-06-26}}</ref>

She is also an elected member of the [[International Statistical Institute]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.isi-web.org/index.php/about-isi/who-is-isi/members/indivual|title=Individual members|publisher=International Statistical Institute|accessdate=2017-11-30|archive-date=29 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170729010059/https://www.isi-web.org/index.php/about-isi/who-is-isi/members/indivual|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== An introduction to GLM ==
She wrote the book ''An introduction to [[generalized linear model]]s''.<ref>{{Cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ZzncBQAAQBAJ |title = An Introduction to Generalized Linear Models|isbn = 9781584889519|last1 = Dobson|first1 = Annette J.|last2 = Barnett|first2 = Adrian |authorlink2=Adrian G. Barnett|date = 12 May 2008| publisher=CRC Press }}</ref>  

== Most highly cited publications ==
*Kuulasmaa K, Tunstall-Pedoe H, Dobson A, Fortmann S, Sans S, Tolonen H, Evans A, Ferrario M, Tuomilehto J. Estimation of contribution of changes in classic risk factors to trends in coronary-event rates across the WHO MONICA Project populations.<ref>Lancet. 2000;355(9205):675–687.</ref>
*Brown WJ, Bryson L, Byles JE, Dobson AJ, Lee C, Mishra G, Schofield M. Women's Health Australia: Recruitment for a national longitudinal cohort study.<ref>Women and Health. 1998;28(1):2340.</ref>
